description: Aeon adversary model. Each entry lists assumed access/knowledge, protected assets at risk, expected defensive response, residual risk, and explicit non-guarantees.
non_guarantees_global: Aeon does NOT claim resistance to a fully compromised processor.
Aeon does NOT claim resistance to compromised firmware below the OS.
Aeon does NOT claim resistance to live physical-memory extraction on general-purpose hardware.
Aeon does NOT claim resistance to hostile hardware (malicious accelerator, backdoored NIC, etc.).
Aeon does NOT claim guaranteed secret erasure from RAM.
Aeon does NOT provide legal, safety, or military certification.

adversaries.name: accidental_operator_error
adversaries.expected_response: config-invariant tests + strict_load metadata gate refuse silent K/vocab/patch/policy drift; recovery via .prev retention.
adversaries.residual_risk: operator can delete .prev + latest ckpt; docs prescribe retention.

adversaries.name: malformed_input
adversaries.expected_response: SentencePiece byte-fallback prevents <unk> tokenizer wedge; F4 filesystem policy caps input size; tokeniser + reader reject binary; forward path is bounded by output_bound + certificate.
adversaries.residual_risk: adversarial-length inputs may cost compute up to F4 seq_len ceiling.

adversaries.name: poisoned_corpus_contribution
adversaries.expected_response: F2 corpus provenance requires per-source origin/license/hash/preprocessing version and inclusion status; F6 data attacks quarantine duplicate-flooding / distribution anomalies; unidentified sources are refused entry.
adversaries.residual_risk: subtle, valid-provenance poisoning by a trusted source is out of scope for structural defence.
non_guarantees: semantic detection of covert bias without human review

adversaries.name: unauthorized_local_user
adversaries.expected_response: F4 filesystem policy denies read of checkpoint / metrics / audit outside the deployment identity; F4 process policy has no shell path.
non_guarantees: defence against local privilege escalation exploits

adversaries.name: compromised_dependency
adversaries.expected_response: F2 dependency policy: pinned versions in pyproject.toml, TCB report enumerates every runtime dep, no auto-install from Aeon runtime, weights_only=True neuters pickle-code paths through torch.load.
adversaries.residual_risk: supply-chain compromise of a pinned dep at build time.
non_guarantees: end-to-end supply-chain attestation without operator SBOM signing

adversaries.name: compromised_update_package
adversaries.expected_response: F2 provenance requires signed source_commit + tokenizer + policy identities; F3 checkpoint compatibility rejects mismatched source_commit / policy identities on load.
adversaries.residual_risk: an update signed under a stolen signing key.
non_guarantees: defence against stolen operator signing keys

adversaries.name: remote_attacker
adversaries.access: network reachable if operator exposes a port
adversaries.expected_response: F4 network policy: certified local mode has ZERO required network use; ordinary training/resume/diagnostics/generation/recovery do not require network. No general outbound client is added.
adversaries.residual_risk: if operator opens a port (out of Aeon's control), only Aeon's containment applies.
non_guarantees: defence when the operator deliberately exposes a network surface

adversaries.name: privileged_host_compromise
adversaries.expected_response: Aeon FAILS CLOSED — root can bypass Aeon's runtime containment; F1 explicitly names this as out-of-scope.
adversaries.residual_risk: TOTAL for confidentiality/integrity of live state.
non_guarantees: runtime integrity guarantees when the host OS is not trusted

adversaries.name: powered_off_device_theft
adversaries.expected_response: F3 confidentiality mode wraps checkpoints in AEAD when the operator supplies a key handle; A21 keys are held OUTSIDE the repository.
adversaries.residual_risk: unencrypted deployments; keys reachable from the same theft.
non_guarantees: defence when keys and encrypted payload are stolen together

adversaries.name: checkpoint_substitution
adversaries.expected_response: F3 authenticated envelope: sha256 sidecar + metadata MAC (when confidentiality mode enabled); strict_load refuses on integrity mismatch.
adversaries.residual_risk: attacker who also controls the sha256 sidecar CAN swap a coherent alternative payload; addressed by MAC (F3.1).
non_guarantees: sha256 alone against an attacker with sidecar write access; use MAC/signature

adversaries.name: checkpoint_rollback
adversaries.expected_response: F3.3 monotonic authorization metadata; strict_load rejects ckpt whose authorized_step < current authorized state when anti-rollback is enabled; explicit recovery operation is the only way to accept a lower state.
adversaries.residual_risk: if anti-rollback is disabled by operator, this defence is off.
non_guarantees: rollback protection when the operator disables anti-rollback

adversaries.name: model_extraction_attempt
adversaries.expected_response: F4 rate limits + resource controls constrain the query budget; F5 CONTAINMENT can cut off analysis on anomalous query patterns.
adversaries.residual_risk: extraction over a very long, patient, under-the-limit interaction is not fully preventable.
non_guarantees: complete prevention of statistical extraction attacks

adversaries.name: resource_exhaustion
adversaries.expected_response: F4.5 resource controls: seq_len cap, batch_size cap, disk ceiling, log rotation, restart-rate limit; F5 SAFE_HALT rather than host exhaustion.
adversaries.residual_risk: attacker with authenticated authority to raise limits.
non_guarantees: defence against an authenticated raise of ceilings

adversaries.name: audit_tampering
adversaries.expected_response: F3 audit records use hash-chained sequence numbers; a break in the chain is detected; audit-storage exhaustion enters SAFE_HALT rather than dropping.
adversaries.residual_risk: attacker able to rewrite the ENTIRE chain including its head can produce a coherent forgery.
non_guarantees: defence against total audit-log rewrite by root

adversaries.name: unauthorized_config_change
adversaries.expected_response: E1 config-invariant tests refuse K/margin/dtype/dual-broadcast drift; F3 strict_load rejects when checkpoint metadata's model_config disagrees with running config.
adversaries.residual_risk: config change that ALSO retrains a matching checkpoint bypasses the mismatch check.
non_guarantees: defence against coordinated config + checkpoint swap

adversaries.name: recovery_state_corruption
adversaries.expected_response: F3 recovery-artifact authentication (sha256 + MAC) equal to primary; F8 recovery exercises refuse to activate corrupted recovery artefact.
non_guarantees: forward progress when EVERY recovery artefact is destroyed

adversaries.name: replay_of_previously_valid_state
adversaries.access: ability to substitute a past authentic file
adversaries.expected_response: F3.3 anti-rollback (authorized_step monotone); F5 message-freshness / sequence-continuity checks refuse stale telemetry.
adversaries.residual_risk: replay of very recent authentic message inside the freshness window.
non_guarantees: defence against replay of a still-fresh authentic message

adversaries.name: incompatible_valid_artifact_injection
adversaries.access: attacker with a legitimately signed but wrong-context artefact
adversaries.expected_response: F2 provenance chain requires every downstream artefact to reference its authenticated inputs; F3 strict_load verifies patch_manifest_version, source_commit, tokenizer_identity, corpus_identity, security_policy identity as a bundle.
adversaries.residual_risk: attacker who forges a matching bundle including all upstream identities.
non_guarantees: defence when every upstream identity check is coordinately forged
